jobs.body_text: Temporary Employment Services Agency (TESA) Information Temporary Employment Services Agency (TESA) Temporary Employement Services Agency (TESA) The Temporary Employment Services Agency (TESA) is an auxiliary operation of The City of Calgary that maintains a complement of staff to provide short-term temporary clerical/administrative support within the organization. Work assignments may arise due to illness, vacation, work backlogs, seasonal spikes in work, delays associated with job postings, or other reasons that generate a demand for short-term employees. All open postings will be advertised on The City careers page at www.calgary.ca/careers . Once you have applied, and are successful, a process of testing and interviewing will take place. Only successful applicants will be notified. What types of assignments are available and how lo​ng are the assignments? The majority of assignments are in the administrative, secretarial, customer service, clerical, reception, financial, accounting, records management and legal administrative fields. Occasionally assignments in other areas become available too. Assignments can vary in length from one day up to three months. Where are the assignments located and do I need a vehicle? The City of Calgary has many locations that TESA employees provide support to. Most locations are accessible using Calgary Transit. All transportation and parking costs are the responsibility of the TESA employee. What are the hours of work? Hours range from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with most shifts being 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required depending on the assignment. jobs.body_text: 911 recruitment Information 911 recruitment 9-1-1 is calling you! We’re looking for people who are passionate about serving our community in a fast-paced and rewarding career. Join our team as an Emergency Communications Officer Emergency Communications Officers are the first point of contact in an emergency. Before the police, fire or ambulance crews arrive, it’s the Emergency Communications Officer who is there, gathering critical information, reassuring the caller, providing life-saving instructions, and making sure the appropriate emergency services are dispatched to the scene. Emergency Communications Officers receive a competitive salary and benefits package, and extensive training and skills required for the role. To assist in determining if this position is right for you, please complete this Self evaluation questionnaire . Apply Now Prerequisites and qualifications You must have the following minimum qualifications on the date you submit your application: A High School diploma or equivalency (e.g. GED) or proof of Canadian equivalent (IQAS, WES). At least 2 years of experience in public sectors such as security, call centre, social work, health care, working with vulnerable populations or emergency-related services. Proficiency with computers; using multiple monitors and systems simultaneously. Keyboarding skills of 35 wpm. The ability to maintain focus, attention to detail, and make critical decisions under pressure. The ability to work in a safety-sensitive position with strict adherence to performance standards and protocols. Preferred qualifications include: Completion of post-secondary education in emergency communications, criminal justice, sociology, psychology, social work or an emergency related field. Prior experience as a 9-1-1 call taker or dispatcher. Experience dealing with crisis situations, mental health interventions, and conflict resolution. Multilingual skills and cultural fluency. Familiarity with emergency dispatch software and real-time data systems (CAD, CPIC, SENTRY, etc). Security requirements: Applicants who advance in the recruitment process are required to undergo an enhanced security clearance and polygraph exam. To be successful at the security phase, applicants must be three years clear of any detected or undetected illegal activity, and must not have any major criminal offences in their background.
